overview.problemStatement: TaskMan must prove who a person is before any workspace data is shown, and must let an account owner cut off access from a device that is lost, stolen or no longer trusted. Email + password accounts are the default path, so registration, address proof and password recovery all have to be safe against replay and against leaking which addresses exist.
overview.proposedSolution: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed (salt rounds 10) in server/src/models/userModel.ts; registration, resend, and password recovery use single-use tokens whose SHA-256 hash is the only thing stored (server/src/utils/tokens.ts). A successful sign-in mints a 7-day JWT carrying a unique jti and a Session row keyed by the token hash (server/src/controllers/authController.ts issueSession, server/src/models/sessionModel.ts). The protect middleware re-checks that session on every request, so logout, password reset and the signed-in devices screen can invalidate a token server-side before it expires.
overview.targetAudience: Everyone with a TaskMan account: new signups who must prove their address, returning members who use several devices, and workspace owners who need a reliable way to end a session.
assumptions: Email delivery goes through Resend when RESEND_API_KEY is set, otherwise SMTP when EMAIL_HOST is set; with neither, only a development build prints the message to the console and a production build throws (server/src/utils/sendEmail.ts).

The documented session lifetime is bounded by the 7-day JWT expiry, and MongoDB removes the Session row about one day after that through the TTL index (expireAfterSeconds 8 days) in server/src/models/sessionModel.ts.
Local password accounts remain the default path for team members; OIDC sign-in is documented separately as the sso-2fa feature.
DEV_AUTO_VERIFY=true is a local convenience flag (read with process.env in authController.isDevAutoVerify) that skips the verification email; production behaviour assumes it is unset.
outOfScope: Single sign-on with Google and Microsoft, two-factor authentication and personal API tokens, which are documented as the sso-2fa feature.
Workspace roles and permissions: GET /api/auth/currentuser reports them, but they are defined and enforced by the workspaces-rbac feature.
Password strength meters, breach-list checks and forced rotation: the only implemented rule is a minimum length of 8 characters (MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH in server/src/controllers/authController.ts).
Profile editing, avatars and notification preferences in server/src/controllers/profileController.ts, which share the router but are not part of authentication.

userStories.title: Create an account with my email address
userStories.role: person signing up for the first time
userStories.want: register with my name, email and a password, and receive a verification email
userStories.benefit: my address is proven before the account can be used

acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /api/auth/signup creates an unverified account and answers 201 with the id, name, email and a requiresVerification flag, and never with the password or any token
A password shorter than 8 characters is rejected with 400, while exactly 8 characters is accepted
Signing up with an address that already has an account answers 400 'User already exists' instead of creating a second account
An invalid email, a missing name, a name longer than 80 characters or a non-string value is answered with 400 and never with a 500

userStories.title: Prove my email address before signing in
userStories.want: open the link that was emailed to me and have the account marked verified
userStories.benefit: the address on the account is one I control

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /api/auth/verify-email/:token marks the account verified and clears the token, and the same link cannot be used twice
Signing in before the address is verified answers 403 with requiresVerification true and issues no session
POST /api/auth/resend-verification answers identically for unknown, already verified and unverified addresses, so it cannot be used to discover accounts

userStories.title: Sign in and stay signed in for a working week
userStories.want: exchange my email and password for a token that the server can revoke
userStories.benefit: I stay signed in across days, and losing a device is recoverable

acceptanceCriteria.text: A successful login returns a token plus the summary fields the web app stores (id, name, email, onboardingComplete, activeWorkspace, activeWorkspaceSlug, workspaces) and no sensitive fields
A wrong password and an unknown address are answered with the same 401 'Invalid email or password'
A NoSQL operator payload such as { "$gt": "" } in the email field is rejected by validation before any query runs
The issued JWT carries a unique jti and expires in 7 days, and the Session row stores only the SHA-256 hash of that token
A request whose token belongs to an invalidated or missing session answers 401 'Session expired or invalidated. Please log in again.'
POST /api/auth/logout invalidates only the session that made the request, so two sign-ins from the same second are unaffected
GET /api/auth/currentuser returns the caller's identity plus workspace, role, permissions and derived actions for the requested workspaceSlug, and answers 403 when the caller is not a member

userStories.title: Reset a password I have forgotten
userStories.role: account owner who cannot sign in
userStories.want: request a link by email and set a new password
userStories.benefit: I regain access without involving an administrator

acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /api/auth/forgot-password answers 200 with the same generic message whether or not the address exists, and sends nothing to an unknown address
An expired reset token is rejected, and only the most recent link for an account is honoured
A completed reset invalidates every session on the account and clears the ssoOnly flag

userStories.title: See the sessions on my account and change my password
userStories.want: list where I am signed in, end one session or all others, and change my password
userStories.benefit: a device I no longer control cannot reach my workspace

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /api/profile/sessions lists the account's active sessions, the current one first, with user agent, IP and timestamps and never with token material
DELETE /api/profile/sessions/:id signs out one device, which can no longer call the API, and 404s an unknown or foreign id
POST /api/profile/sessions/revoke-others signs out every other device and keeps the session that made the request
One account can never see or revoke the sessions of another account
PUT /api/profile/password rejects a wrong current password with 401 and changes nothing
A successful password change keeps the session that made the request and revokes every other session of the account

userStories.title: Finish onboarding and get a first workspace
userStories.want: save my onboarding answers and have a workspace created with me as its Product Owner
userStories.benefit: I can start planning work straight after signing up

acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /api/auth/onboarding stores the answers with a completedAt timestamp, creates a workspace whose slug is derived from the name and assigns the Product Owner system role, defaulting the name to "<name>'s Workspace"
A second onboarding call is idempotent and returns the existing workspace instead of creating another one
A non-string or over-long workspaceName, or an onboarding answer longer than 80 characters, is answered with 400 rather than 500

functionalRequirements.text: POST /api/auth/signup creates an account from name, email and password, normalises the email to lower case, refuses a duplicate address and answers with a summary that omits the password and tokens (server/src/controllers/authController.ts registerUser, validateSignup)

Email verification stores only the hash of a 32-byte random token with a 24-hour expiry, emails a link built from CLIENT_URL, and answers the same generic message when the address is unknown or already verified (authController.verifyEmail, resendVerification; server/src/utils/tokens.ts createSecureToken)

A verified account with the right password is issued a JWT signed with the configured jwtSecret, carrying a random jti and a 7-day expiry, together with a Session document that points at the user, user agent, IP address and the SHA-256 hash of the token only (authController.generateToken, createSession, issueSession)

Login failures are uniform: validation errors and a wrong password both produce 401 'Invalid email or password', unknown accounts and operator payloads cannot be distinguished, and the email lookups are written as { email: { $eq: String(email) } } so a payload object cannot be cast into a query operator

The protect middleware verifies the bearer JWT, then requires a Session row matching the token hash with isValid true, refreshes lastLoggedIn at most once every 5 minutes and attaches the user document without the password (server/src/middleware/authMiddleware.ts)
POST /api/auth/logout reads the bearer token, marks exactly that session invalid and always answers 200 'Logged out successfully' (authController.logoutUser)

POST /api/auth/forgot-password stores a hashed reset token with a 1-hour expiry and answers 200 with the same wording for known and unknown addresses; POST /api/auth/reset-password/:token consumes it once and sets the new password (authController.forgotPassword, resetPassword)

Credential changes end sessions that must end: a completed reset invalidates every session of the account and clears ssoOnly, and a password change from Settings keeps the current session while revoking the others (authController.resetPassword, profileController.changePassword)

The signed-in devices API lists only the caller's active sessions with a current flag, revokes one session by id, or revokes all others while keeping the calling session (server/src/controllers/profileController.ts listSessions, revokeSession, revokeOtherSessions with activeSessionFilter)

POST /api/auth/onboarding records the onboarding answers, is idempotent once a workspace exists, generates a unique slug and a 12-hex invite code, assigns the Product Owner system role to the creator and sets the workspace active (authController.saveOnboarding, generateSlug)

GET /api/auth/currentuser resolves the signed-in identity together with the requested workspace, the caller's role, the role's permissions and the derived action list, and self-heals a membership without roleId by assigning Product Owner to the workspace owner and Viewer to anyone else (authController.getCurrentUser, deriveActions)

The web app keeps the token and the user summary in one place (client/src/utils/session.ts), clears the in-memory query cache and the service-worker API cache on any new login or logout, and the shared axios client clears the session and redirects to /login?expired=1 on a 401 that is not an auth call (client/src/utils/api.ts)

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Authentication traffic is rate limited: the whole /api/auth area is capped at 100 requests per 15 minutes per IP, and login, forgot-password, resend-verification, password change and the two-factor routes share a stricter 20-per-15-minute limiter (server/src/app.ts authLimiter, sensitiveLimiter), satisfying CON-511 and CON-514

No credential or token is stored in a form that can be replayed or read back: passwords are bcrypt hashes, and verification, reset and session tokens exist in the database only as SHA-256 digests (server/src/models/userModel.ts pre-save hook, server/src/utils/tokens.ts hashToken), satisfying CON-505 and CON-511

Every mutating auth route declares an express-validator chain (validateSignup, validateLogin, validateForgotPassword, validateResetPassword, validateResendVerification) and controllers cast user input with String() before querying, so malformed payloads answer 400 instead of crashing with a 500 (CON-515, CON-516)

The behaviour above is covered by Jest unit tests for the pure helpers and by integration tests against a real MongoDB for the flows (CON-402, CON-403, CON-404); the commands are pnpm --filter server test and pnpm --filter server test:integration

edgeCases.description: A verification link is opened after its 24-hour expiry, or a second time
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: GET /api/auth/verify-email/:token answers 400 explaining the link was already used or expired and pointing at login and a fresh link

edgeCases.description: A reset link is requested twice and the older one is used
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The second request overwrites the stored hash, so only the newest link works (verified by passwordReset.test.ts 'only honours the most recent reset link')

edgeCases.description: Two logins happen within the same second and one of them logs out
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The jti on each JWT plus the token hash on the session make the two sessions distinct, so logout kills exactly one of them

edgeCases.description: The email provider is down or not configured
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The account is still created; the failure is logged, the verification link is printed only when NODE_ENV is not production, and a production process without a provider throws instead of silently dropping mail

edgeCases.description: A session row is older than the JWT lifetime
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The token can no longer be verified by JWT expiry, the row is excluded from the signed-in devices list by activeSessionFilter, and the TTL index removes it about a day later

edgeCases.description: A revoked session replays its token
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: protect finds no session with isValid true and answers 401 'Session expired or invalidated. Please log in again.'

edgeCases.description: A request sends a number, object or null as the password on signup or reset
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The validator rejects the payload with 400 and the controller never calls bcrypt with a non-string value

edgeCases.description: An account resets its password while another device is signed in
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The other device's session is invalidated by resetPassword and its next request answers 401, sending the browser to /login?expired=1

dependencies.name: jsonwebtoken
dependencies.notes: Signs the 7-day session JWT with a jti (server/src/controllers/authController.ts)

dependencies.name: bcryptjs
dependencies.notes: Password hashing with 10 salt rounds and comparison in userModel.matchPassword

dependencies.name: express-validator
dependencies.notes: Validation chains exported from authController and attached in routes/authRoutes.ts

dependencies.name: express-rate-limit
dependencies.notes: authLimiter, apiLimiter and sensitiveLimiter in server/src/app.ts

dependencies.name: mongoose
dependencies.notes: User and Session models, including the Session TTL index

dependencies.name: nodemailer
dependencies.notes: SMTP transport used when EMAIL_HOST is configured

dependencies.name: Resend HTTP API
dependencies.notes: Preferred email provider; needs RESEND_API_KEY and a verified domain for arbitrary recipients

dependencies.name: SMTP provider
dependencies.notes: Fallback provider configured with EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_USER and EMAIL_PASS

dependencies.name: MongoDB
dependencies.notes: Stores the users and the revocable session rows

dependencies.name: server/src/config/env.ts
dependencies.notes: Validates JWT_SECRET, MONGO_URI, CLIENT_URL and the rate-limit and proxy settings before the app starts

risks.description: Verification and reset emails are filtered as spam, so an account can never be activated
risks.mitigation: A resend endpoint exists, the account still works after a later verification, and the development console prints the link when no provider is configured

risks.description: Session documents accumulate and make the authenticated lookup slow
risks.mitigation: The index on { token: 1 } makes the hash lookup unique and the TTL index (8 days) deletes expired rows

risks.description: A database copy is replayed against the API
risks.mitigation: Only SHA-256 token hashes are stored, passwords are bcrypt hashes, and every session can be invalidated from the users own settings

risks.description: Rate limiting keys on the wrong address behind a reverse proxy, weakening brute-force protection
risks.mitigation: app.set('trust proxy', config.trustProxy) is applied when the environment declares a proxy depth (server/src/app.ts, server/src/config/env.ts)
